If old_string appears multiple times, provide a more specific old_string or set replace_all to true. Non-zero exits are reported as `[exit code: N]` markers; investigate failures before moving on. On Windows a killed process settles as `[exit code: 1]` without a signal marker; treat a bare exit 1 after an interruption as a termination, not a command failure.

After session resume or fork, an active goal is disarmed: when a human asks to continue or resume in any wording or language, use update_goal action resume to rearm it. Use same-session goal tools for ordinary long-running objectives, and plain subagents or workflows for bounded delegation and fan-out.

Set `run_in_background: false` only when your next action depends on that subagent's result. tools.name: glob
tools.description: Find files whose paths match a glob pattern. Returns matching file paths — never directories — including hidden and ignored files (VCS metadata directories are excluded). Up to 100 paths come back in modification-time order; a larger result returns the first 100 paths in modification-time order, says so, and reports where the complete sorted list was saved. This tool does not enumerate directory entries.

tools.name: interrupt_agent
tools.description: Request cancellation of a background agent's current turn by its agent id. The target may be your direct child or a deeper agent created under you. Only the current turn stops: messages already queued for the agent stay parked until a later send_message, agents it started keep running, and the agent itself stays available for follow-ups. This call returns as soon as the stop request is accepted, so the target may keep running briefly; interrupting an agent that already finished is an accepted no-op.

agent_id.description: The agent id of the running agent to interrupt.

tools.name: job_kill
tools.description: Request cancellation of a running background job by job id. Returns immediately; the job settles as killed once its work actually stops.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

reason.description: Optional short reason, recorded in the log and forwarded to the job.

tools.name: job_list
tools.description: List your background jobs (running and finished) with their ids, kinds, and statuses.

tools.name: job_output
tools.description: Read a background job. Stream jobs return only output since the previous read; final-output jobs return their result after settlement. Every response ends with `[status: ...]`. Reads are non-blocking unless `wait: true`, which waits up to the configured cap.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

wait.description: Block until the job reaches a terminal status or the timeout expires. A timed-out wait returns [status: running] and leaves the job alive.

timeout_ms.description: Max wait in milliseconds (only meaningful with wait: true). Defaults to the configured wait timeout; capped by the configured maximum.

tools.name: list_agents
tools.description: List your continuable background subagents by durable id and label. Use it to recall which ones you started, not to poll for completion — you are told when one finishes. Status comes from the live registry: running means the agent is working right now, idle means it is loaded but between turns (it may be waiting on agents it started), and ready means it exists only in storage — resumable, not terminal, and not a result waiting to be collected; a `send_message` starts a new turn on the same conversation, and a direct child remains a `send_message` candidate in every status. The snapshot is not a delivery promise — `send_message` performs the authoritative check and may still fail. Children that could not be read are reported as diagnostics instead of being silently dropped. Scope `descendants` walks the whole tree below you in stable pre-order, annotating each entry with its durable direct-parent session id and depth. You may use `send_message` only for depth-1 entries; deeper entries are candidates for `interrupt_agent` only.

scope.description: children (default) lists direct children only; descendants walks the complete tree below you.

tools.name: pwsh
tools.description: Execute a PowerShell command (`pwsh -Command`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh pwsh process: no state (cwd, variables, functions) persists between calls — pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Paths use native Windows form (`C:\...`); read environment variables with `$env:NAME`. Non-zero exits are reported as `[exit code: N]`. Current harness environment facts are exposed through managed `$env:DSH_*` variables; inspect them when needed. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]` — a policy denial, not a bug in the command; do not retry another way. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. On Windows a force-killed command settles as `[exit code: 1]` without a signal marker — treat it as an interruption, not a command failure. Set `run_in_background: true` for long-running commands: the call returns a job id immediately; read its output with `job_output` and stop it with `job_kill`. Under the Windows sandbox, read-only pwsh runs in PowerShell ConstrainedLanguage mode, while workspace-write stays in FullLanguage unless host policy says otherwise. In read-only, prefer cmdlets and core types (`[string]`, `[datetime]`, `[regex]`, `[guid]`); .NET static calls (`[System.IO.*]::`, `[math]::`), `Add-Type`, COM objects, and reflection fail with "only core types" errors. `-f` formatting, property access, and core cmdlets work. In both confined modes, programs cannot open named pipes, so a command that captures another program's output through piped stdio (Node.js `child_process.spawn`/`exec` with the default `stdio: 'pipe'`) fails with EPERM, while `stdio: 'inherit'` and `stdio: 'ignore'` spawns work and PowerShell's own pipelines are unaffected. That EPERM is the documented boundary: do not retry the command another way — escalate the exact command once or restructure it to avoid capturing output. Attempting a command the sandbox may deny is safe and expected: run it and read the marker rather than assuming the denial. When a command is denied and a wider mode would let it succeed, escalate immediately in the same turn — the one sanctioned exception to a denial: retry the exact same command once with `sandbox_permissions` (the narrowest wider mode that suffices) plus a one-sentence `justification`. Do not detour through chat to ask permission first — the approval prompt raised by that retry is how the user consents. If the session states approval prompts are disabled, there is no exception: a denial is final — do not set `sandbox_permissions`. Never escalate speculatively: ground the request in a real denial — normally the one this command just hit; escalating up front is fine only when this session already denied the same access. A rejected escalation is final for that command — stop and explain, never work around it — but it does not forbid attempting or escalating other commands later.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "Get-Process" → "List running processes".

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap, and kills the command on expiry.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

run_in_background.description: Run in the background and return a job id immediately (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). No timeout applies.

sandbox_permissions.description: The wider sandbox mode this command needs. Only valid as a one-shot retry of a command the sandbox just denied; requires justification and user approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact command needs the wider access.

tools.name: ralph
tools.description: Run a foreground fresh-agent Ralph loop toward one immutable objective. Use only when the direct human explicitly asks for Ralph or fresh-agent iteration. Each round opens a new child with no parent conversation or prior child session; the shared workspace is long-term memory, and only a bounded structured report crosses rounds. The call returns when a worker reports completion or a concrete blocker, or at the round limit. Ordinary long-running same-session work belongs to goal tools.

objective.description: The immutable completion objective for every fresh Ralph round.

maxRounds.description: Optional positive safe-integer round cap, bounded by the deployment ceiling.

tools.name: read
tools.description: Read a UTF-8 text file and return line-numbered content.

file_path.description: Path to read, resolved by the filesystem backend.

offset.description: 1-based first line to return. Defaults to 1.

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to return. Defaults to 2000.

tools.name: read_image
tools.description: Read a PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF file and return the image itself. Requires the current model to accept image input.

file_path.description: Path to the image file, resolved by the filesystem backend.

tools.name: send_message
tools.description: Send a message to a background subagent by its subagent id, continuing the same conversation. It becomes the subagent's next turn: if it is still working, the message waits until its current turn finishes, so it cannot redirect work already underway. This call returns no answer from the subagent — only confirmation that the message was delivered — so use it to give it more work. A failure means the message was NOT delivered.

subagent_id.description: The subagent id returned when the background subagent was started.

message.description: The message to deliver to the subagent.

tools.name: skill
tools.description: Load the full instructions for an available skill. Call this with the exact skill name from the session skill catalog before acting on a task that names or clearly matches that skill.

name.description: The exact skill name from the available skills list.

tools.name: subagent
tools.description: Delegate a self-contained task to a subagent (a separate agent that works in its own context) to offload focused, independent work — research, a scoped implementation, an analysis — so it does not consume this conversation's context. The subagent returns its result, not its intermediate steps. Give it a complete, standalone prompt: it does not see this conversation. This tool runs in the background by default, immediately returns a durable subagent id, and keeps the child conversation available for later turns. When that run settles, the runtime sends the parent a notice containing its outcome and any final assistant message; `send_message` starts a later turn in the same child conversation. Set `run_in_background: false` only when your next action depends on receiving the result.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the delegated task, for display.

prompt.description: The complete, self-contained task for the subagent. It does not share this conversation's context, so include everything it needs.

run_in_background.description: Whether to run in the background and return a durable subagent id immediately. Defaults to true. Set false to wait for the result when your next action depends on it.

tools.name: subagent_fork
tools.description: Delegate a task to a subagent that inherits this conversation: a child agent seeded with all completed turns so far (it does not see the current in-flight turn). Use this when the subtask builds on this conversation's context — a follow-up analysis, a review, a continuation — without consuming this conversation's context for the work itself. You receive its result, not its intermediate steps. This tool runs in the background by default, immediately returns a durable subagent id, and keeps the child conversation available for later turns. When that run settles, the runtime sends the parent a notice containing its outcome and any final assistant message; `send_message` starts a later turn in the same child conversation. Set `run_in_background: false` only when your next action depends on receiving the result.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the delegated task, for display.

prompt.description: The task for the subagent. It already sees this conversation's completed turns, so build on them freely and state only what is new.

run_in_background.description: Whether to run in the background and return a durable subagent id immediately. Defaults to true. Set false to wait for the result when your next action depends on it.

tools.name: todo_write
tools.description: Record and update a structured task list for the current work. Send the ENTIRE list every call — it REPLACES the previous list (there are no partial updates, no per-item edits). Use it to plan multi-step work and show progress: add one todo per concrete step before you start. Mark every todo being actively worked on `in_progress` — several at once when work genuinely runs in parallel (e.g. concurrent subagents or background commands), one for sequential work; while work remains, at least one task should be `in_progress`. Mark a todo `completed` the moment it is done (do not batch completions), and allow no `in_progress` item only once all work is complete. Skip the list for trivial single-step tasks. Statuses: `pending` (not started), `in_progress` (being worked on now), `completed` (finished).

todos.description: The COMPLETE task list, replacing any previous list.

content.description: What the task is — a short imperative line.

tools.name: update_goal
tools.description: Update the exact current goal revision. edit, pause, and resume require a direct top-level human request. During an automatic continuation of the current goal, complete and blocked are also allowed. blocked is rejected before the configured minimum round count; the model remains responsible for judging that the same condition persisted across those rounds and must explain it in blocked_reason.

revision.description: Exact positive revision returned by get_goal.

objective.description: Replacement objective; valid only with action edit.

max_goal_rounds.description: Replacement cap; valid only with action edit.

blocked_reason.description: Concrete blocking condition; required only with action blocked.

tools.name: web_search
tools.description: Search the web for current information. Returns an optional summary answer and a list of source URLs.

tools.name: workflow
tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

The workflow's identity rides the `meta` parameter as JSON: required `name` (short kebab-case) and `description` strings, optional `whenToUse` string and `phases` array (`{title, detail?, provider?, model?}`). The `script` parameter is the plain JavaScript body ONLY (NOT TypeScript, and NO `export const meta` statement — meta is a parameter, not code), running with top-level await; end with `return <value>` — the value must be JSON-serializable and is this tool's result.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf — no pattern/format/numeric bounds) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides (either may be provided alone). Anything else (`effort`/`isolation`/`agentType`) is rejected loudly.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. An ordinary stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) throw errors that ALWAYS kill the script — they never dissolve into a per-item `null`.

Constraints: concurrency and total-agent caps apply; no filesystem, network, timers, or Node.js APIs are provided — the agents do the work, the script only coordinates them. The run executes in the foreground: this call returns when the whole script finishes.

script.description: The plain-JS workflow script body (top-level await allowed; NO `export const meta` statement; end with `return <json-value>`).

meta.description: The workflow identity block (plain JSON — never code).

description.description: One-line description of what the workflow does.

whenToUse.description: Optional guidance on when this workflow applies.

phases.description: Optional phase declarations matched by phase() calls.

title.description: The phase title phase() calls match by exact string.

detail.description: Optional one-line description of the phase.

provider.description: Optional provider override this phase is expected to use.

model.description: Optional model override this phase is expected to use.

args.description: Optional JSON input exposed to the script as the `args` global (wrap a bare list as a field, e.g. {"files": [...]}).

tools.description: Create or fully replace a UTF-8 text file.

file_path.description: Path to write, resolved by the filesystem backend.

content.description: Full UTF-8 text content to write.

sandbox_permissions.description: The wider sandbox mode this file operation needs. Only valid as a one-shot retry of an operation the sandbox just denied; requires justification and user approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact file operation needs the wider access.

wait.description: Block until the job reaches a terminal status or the timeout expires. A timed-out wait returns [status: running] and leaves the job alive.

timeout_ms.description: Max wait in milliseconds (only meaningful with wait: true). Defaults to the configured wait timeout; capped by the configured maximum.

tools.name: list_agents
tools.description: List your continuable background subagents by durable id and label. Use it to recall which ones you started, not to poll for completion — you are told when one finishes. Status comes from the live registry: running means the agent is working right now, idle means it is loaded but between turns (it may be waiting on agents it started), and ready means it exists only in storage — resumable, not terminal, and not a result waiting to be collected; a `send_message` starts a new turn on the same conversation, and a direct child remains a `send_message` candidate in every status. The snapshot is not a delivery promise — `send_message` performs the authoritative check and may still fail. Children that could not be read are reported as diagnostics instead of being silently dropped. Scope `descendants` walks the whole tree below you in stable pre-order, annotating each entry with its durable direct-parent session id and depth. You may use `send_message` only for depth-1 entries; deeper entries are candidates for `interrupt_agent` only.

scope.description: children (default) lists direct children only; descendants walks the complete tree below you.

tools.name: pwsh
tools.description: Execute a PowerShell command (`pwsh -Command`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh pwsh process: no state (cwd, variables, functions) persists between calls — pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Paths use native Windows form (`C:\...`); read environment variables with `$env:NAME`. Non-zero exits are reported as `[exit code: N]`. Current harness environment facts are exposed through managed `$env:DSH_*` variables; inspect them when needed. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]` — a policy denial, not a bug in the command; do not retry another way. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. On Windows a force-killed command settles as `[exit code: 1]` without a signal marker — treat it as an interruption, not a command failure. Set `run_in_background: true` for long-running commands: the call returns a job id immediately; read its output with `job_output` and stop it with `job_kill`. Under the Windows sandbox, read-only pwsh runs in PowerShell ConstrainedLanguage mode, while workspace-write stays in FullLanguage unless host policy says otherwise. In read-only, prefer cmdlets and core types (`[string]`, `[datetime]`, `[regex]`, `[guid]`); .NET static calls (`[System.IO.*]::`, `[math]::`), `Add-Type`, COM objects, and reflection fail with "only core types" errors. `-f` formatting, property access, and core cmdlets work. In both confined modes, programs cannot open named pipes, so a command that captures another program's output through piped stdio (Node.js `child_process.spawn`/`exec` with the default `stdio: 'pipe'`) fails with EPERM, while `stdio: 'inherit'` and `stdio: 'ignore'` spawns work and PowerShell's own pipelines are unaffected. That EPERM is the documented boundary: do not retry the command another way — escalate the exact command once or restructure it to avoid capturing output. Attempting a command the sandbox may deny is safe and expected: run it and read the marker rather than assuming the denial. When a command is denied and a wider mode would let it succeed, escalate immediately in the same turn — the one sanctioned exception to a denial: retry the exact same command once with `sandbox_permissions` (the narrowest wider mode that suffices) plus a one-sentence `justification`. Do not detour through chat to ask permission first — the approval prompt raised by that retry is how the user consents. If the session states approval prompts are disabled, there is no exception: a denial is final — do not set `sandbox_permissions`. Never escalate speculatively: ground the request in a real denial — normally the one this command just hit; escalating up front is fine only when this session already denied the same access. A rejected escalation is final for that command — stop and explain, never work around it — but it does not forbid attempting or escalating other commands later.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "Get-Process" → "List running processes".

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap, and kills the command on expiry.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

run_in_background.description: Run in the background and return a job id immediately (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). No timeout applies.

sandbox_permissions.description: The wider sandbox mode this command needs. Only valid as a one-shot retry of a command the sandbox just denied; requires justification and user approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact command needs the wider access.

tools.name: ralph
tools.description: Run a foreground fresh-agent Ralph loop toward one immutable objective. Use only when the direct human explicitly asks for Ralph or fresh-agent iteration. Each round opens a new child with no parent conversation or prior child session; the shared workspace is long-term memory, and only a bounded structured report crosses rounds. The call returns when a worker reports completion or a concrete blocker, or at the round limit. Ordinary long-running same-session work belongs to goal tools.

objective.description: The immutable completion objective for every fresh Ralph round.

maxRounds.description: Optional positive safe-integer round cap, bounded by the deployment ceiling.

tools.name: read
tools.description: Read a UTF-8 text file and return line-numbered content.

file_path.description: Path to read, resolved by the filesystem backend.

offset.description: 1-based first line to return. Defaults to 1.

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to return. Defaults to 2000.

tools.name: read_image

tools.name: send_message
tools.description: Send a message to a background subagent by its subagent id, continuing the same conversation. It becomes the subagent's next turn: if it is still working, the message waits until its current turn finishes, so it cannot redirect work already underway. This call returns no answer from the subagent — only confirmation that the message was delivered — so use it to give it more work. A failure means the message was NOT delivered.

subagent_id.description: The subagent id returned when the background subagent was started.

message.description: The message to deliver to the subagent.

tools.name: skill
tools.description: Load the full instructions for an available skill. Call this with the exact skill name from the session skill catalog before acting on a task that names or clearly matches that skill.

name.description: The exact skill name from the available skills list.

tools.name: subagent
tools.description: Delegate a self-contained task to a subagent (a separate agent that works in its own context) to offload focused, independent work — research, a scoped implementation, an analysis — so it does not consume this conversation's context. The subagent returns its result, not its intermediate steps. Give it a complete, standalone prompt: it does not see this conversation. This tool runs in the background by default, immediately returns a durable subagent id, and keeps the child conversation available for later turns. When that run settles, the runtime sends the parent a notice containing its outcome and any final assistant message; `send_message` starts a later turn in the same child conversation. Set `run_in_background: false` only when your next action depends on receiving the result.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the delegated task, for display.

prompt.description: The complete, self-contained task for the subagent. It does not share this conversation's context, so include everything it needs.

run_in_background.description: Whether to run in the background and return a durable subagent id immediately. Defaults to true. Set false to wait for the result when your next action depends on it.

tools.name: subagent_fork
tools.description: Delegate a task to a subagent that inherits this conversation: a child agent seeded with all completed turns so far (it does not see the current in-flight turn). Use this when the subtask builds on this conversation's context — a follow-up analysis, a review, a continuation — without consuming this conversation's context for the work itself. You receive its result, not its intermediate steps. This tool runs in the background by default, immediately returns a durable subagent id, and keeps the child conversation available for later turns. When that run settles, the runtime sends the parent a notice containing its outcome and any final assistant message; `send_message` starts a later turn in the same child conversation. Set `run_in_background: false` only when your next action depends on receiving the result.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the delegated task, for display.

prompt.description: The task for the subagent. It already sees this conversation's completed turns, so build on them freely and state only what is new.

run_in_background.description: Whether to run in the background and return a durable subagent id immediately. Defaults to true. Set false to wait for the result when your next action depends on it.

tools.name: todo_write
tools.description: Record and update a structured task list for the current work. Send the ENTIRE list every call — it REPLACES the previous list (there are no partial updates, no per-item edits). Use it to plan multi-step work and show progress: add one todo per concrete step before you start. Mark every todo being actively worked on `in_progress` — several at once when work genuinely runs in parallel (e.g. concurrent subagents or background commands), one for sequential work; while work remains, at least one task should be `in_progress`. Mark a todo `completed` the moment it is done (do not batch completions), and allow no `in_progress` item only once all work is complete. Skip the list for trivial single-step tasks. Statuses: `pending` (not started), `in_progress` (being worked on now), `completed` (finished).

todos.description: The COMPLETE task list, replacing any previous list.

content.description: What the task is — a short imperative line.

tools.name: update_goal
tools.description: Update the exact current goal revision. edit, pause, and resume require a direct top-level human request. During an automatic continuation of the current goal, complete and blocked are also allowed. blocked is rejected before the configured minimum round count; the model remains responsible for judging that the same condition persisted across those rounds and must explain it in blocked_reason.

revision.description: Exact positive revision returned by get_goal.

objective.description: Replacement objective; valid only with action edit.

max_goal_rounds.description: Replacement cap; valid only with action edit.

blocked_reason.description: Concrete blocking condition; required only with action blocked.

tools.name: web_search
tools.description: Search the web for current information. Returns an optional summary answer and a list of source URLs.

tools.name: workflow
tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

The workflow's identity rides the `meta` parameter as JSON: required `name` (short kebab-case) and `description` strings, optional `whenToUse` string and `phases` array (`{title, detail?, provider?, model?}`). The `script` parameter is the plain JavaScript body ONLY (NOT TypeScript, and NO `export const meta` statement — meta is a parameter, not code), running with top-level await; end with `return <value>` — the value must be JSON-serializable and is this tool's result.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf — no pattern/format/numeric bounds) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides (either may be provided alone). Anything else (`effort`/`isolation`/`agentType`) is rejected loudly.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. An ordinary stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) throw errors that ALWAYS kill the script — they never dissolve into a per-item `null`.

Constraints: concurrency and total-agent caps apply; no filesystem, network, timers, or Node.js APIs are provided — the agents do the work, the script only coordinates them. The run executes in the foreground: this call returns when the whole script finishes.

script.description: The plain-JS workflow script body (top-level await allowed; NO `export const meta` statement; end with `return <json-value>`).

meta.description: The workflow identity block (plain JSON — never code).

description.description: One-line description of what the workflow does.

whenToUse.description: Optional guidance on when this workflow applies.

phases.description: Optional phase declarations matched by phase() calls.

title.description: The phase title phase() calls match by exact string.

detail.description: Optional one-line description of the phase.

provider.description: Optional provider override this phase is expected to use.

model.description: Optional model override this phase is expected to use.

args.description: Optional JSON input exposed to the script as the `args` global (wrap a bare list as a field, e.g. {"files": [...]}).

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact file operation needs the wider access.

block.text:
The map data is huge — coordinates are hand-placed with lots of crossing lines. The user wants me to rearrange all maps so that lines are straight (orthogonal, box-to-box like a grid), not "lines everywhere".

This is a big task. The coordinates for each city (CHENG_POS) are manually positioned, and lines connect rooms based on `exits`. The lines are straight diagonal lines between arbitrary coordinates, which produces a "messy" look.

The user's request #3: "地图的连线太乱了，根本不像个Mud游戏，我要你重新排列所有地图，要求直线，方框平着连着方框，而不是现在这样哪里都有线条" — rearrange all maps so that connections are straight lines, boxes connect flat to boxes (like orthogonal/Manhattan routing), not lines everywhere.

The best approach that doesn't require hand-placing hundreds of coordinates: **auto-layout the rooms on a grid** based on their connectivity. I can write an algorithm that:
1. For each layer (zhou, each cheng, each bld), compute a grid layout from the exits graph
2. Draw lines as orthogonal (Manhattan) paths: horizontal then vertical (or L-shaped) lines so connections look like "boxes connected flat to boxes"

Actually, "直线，方框平着连着方框" means straight lines, boxes side by side connected flat. The ideal MUD map look: rooms as boxes/squares on a grid, connected by straight orthogonal lines (axis-aligned), no diagonal crisscross.

Approach:
1. Keep the CHENG_POS data as-is (it's the source of room membership per city).
2. But replace rendering of lines with **orthogonal routing** (L-shaped/Manhattan) — draw horizontal-then-vertical segments instead of diagonal lines.
3. Re-layout node positions: compute new positions using a grid-based auto-layout per layer so boxes are aligned in rows/columns.

Actually the cleanest: write an auto-layout function `layoutLayerRooms(rooms, exits)` that assigns each room a grid cell using BFS layers from the entry, and produces coordinates on a grid (e.g., cell 150x150). Then draw lines as orthogonal polylines (h then v) between centers.

But the room coordinates are also used elsewhere: `mapSize()`, `mapZoomReset`, `mapLocate`, `CHENG_POS[game.cheng]`, `enterBld`, etc. The CHENG_POS data is referenced in several places (lines 4745, 4808, 4823, 5316). Also NPC positions? Let me check where CHENG_POS is used.

block.text:
Now I have a good understanding of the layout. Let me now understand the request in detail:

1. **赶路按钮太小，地图本来也小，要么就把移动按钮放在下面，地图依旧支持点击移动，移动按钮移动到折叠下方，做一个四项移动（上下左右）的按钮** — The travel button is too small and the map is small. Either: put movement buttons below, map still supports click-move, move the movement buttons below the fold button, and make a 4-directional (up/down/left/right) button.

So they want a 4-directional D-pad (up/down/left/right) for movement, placed below the fold (折叠) button area, i.e., at the bottom of the interact area or between map and log. The map should still support click-to-move.

2. **怎么回血，怎么使用物品，怎么穿戴装备？疗伤按钮呢？调养呢？** — How to heal HP, how to use items, how to equip gear? Where's the heal button? Where's 调养 (rest/recuperate)?

So I need to make these actions discoverable and accessible. There IS a btn-heal (疗伤) button in the side nav already, and restAtInn (客栈歇宿). There's useItem with commands. But the user can't figure out how to heal/use items/equip. So I should add a proper "行囊/背包" (backpack) panel where they can use consumables and equip items, plus a 疗伤/调养 button in the interact area.

Let me look for an existing backpack/use-item UI. There's line 7852 `go.addEventListener('click',function(){ useItem(sel.value); ...})` — that seems to be a battle item select. Let me search for a full inventory panel.

3. **地图的连线太乱了，根本不像个Mud游戏，我要你重新排列所有地图，要求直线，方框平着连着方框，而不是现在这样哪里都有线条** — Map connections too messy. Rearrange all maps so connections are straight lines, boxes connected flat-to-flat (grid-like orthogonal), not lines everywhere.

This is a big task. The map lines are drawn as straight diagonal lines between arbitrary coordinates. The user wants grid-style layout: rooms placed in a grid, connections only between orthogonal neighbors (up/down/left/right), so lines are straight horizontal/vertical.

The most robust approach: **auto-layout** the rooms on a grid based on connectivity (like a graph layout), instead of manually tweaking CHENG_POS coordinates. But changing coordinates affects a lot (they're stored in data). Better approach: at render time, compute new positions for rooms in each layer using an orthogonal/grid layout algorithm, and draw lines as orthogonal (Manhattan) paths between adjacent boxes.

Actually, the user says "重新排列所有地图，要求直线，方框平着连着方框" — rearrange all maps, require straight lines, boxes connected flat to boxes. So they want:
- Nodes as boxes (方框) 
- Lines straight (horizontal/vertical), box-to-box
- Not crisscrossing lines everywhere

Given the sheer number of rooms (CHENG_POS has hundreds of entries across ~24 cities), manually re-laying out coordinates is infeasible. The best approach is a **procedural grid layout** computed from the room graph at render time:

1. For each layer (zhou / cheng / nei), compute a graph of rooms (nodes) and exits (edges).
2. Lay out the graph on a grid using BFS layers from the entry point (or a spanning tree), assigning each room a grid cell (col, row). 
3. Draw nodes as rounded rectangles (方框) at cell centers, with spacing e.g. 170x140.
4. Draw connections as orthogonal polylines (horizontal then vertical, or L-shaped/elbow) between box centers, so they're straight axis-aligned lines. Use "Z" or "L" routing to avoid overlapping.

Actually, drawing L-shaped routes for every edge can still look messy. **Fix 1: 赶路按钮太小，地图本来也小，要么就把移动按钮放在下面，地图依旧支持点击移动，移动按钮移动到折叠下方，做一个四项移动（上下左右）的按钮**
- The travel buttons are too small, map is small too. Either put the movement buttons below, map still supports click-to-move, move the movement buttons below the fold button, make a 4-direction (up/down/left/right) button.
- So: Add a D-pad style 4-direction movement button (上/下/左/右) below the fold (折叠) area. Map still supports clicking to move.

The map-tip currently shows inline buttons (疾行/逐格/取消) at the bottom of the map. The user says 赶路按钮太小 (travel buttons too small) — this likely refers to the tip-go/tip-btn buttons in the map-tip, which are small. And the map is small too.

The request: "要么就把移动按钮放在下面，地图依旧支持点击移动，移动按钮移动到折叠下方，做一个四项移动（上下左右）的按钮" — "Either put the movement buttons below, the map still supports click-move, the movement buttons move below the fold, make a 4-direction (up/down/left/right) button."

So I should:
1. Add a 4-direction D-pad (上/下/左/右) below the fold button (i.e., below #place-head, or at the bottom of #interact, or below the map panel — "折叠下方" means below the fold button).
2. The 4-direction buttons move the player one step in that direction (using the room's exits: n/s/e/w → 北/南/东/西).
3. Keep map click-to-move as is.

Let me think about "折叠下方" — the fold button is `fold-info` (▾ 折叠) in `#place-head`. So the movement buttons should go below that area — probably between the map and the interact area, or right under place-head. Actually re-reading: "移动按钮移动到折叠下方" — move the movement buttons below the fold. The current "移动按钮" are the map-tip inline buttons (疾行/逐格/取消) shown over the map bottom. The user wants them moved below the fold (i.e., out of the map, into a dedicated area under the map), AND additionally wants a 4-direction D-pad.

I'll design:
- Keep map click-to-move (click node → askMove → move).
- Add a "赶路" button group (D-pad): a 2x2 or cross layout with 上/左/右/下 buttons (and maybe center = 原地歇息? No, keep simple). These buttons move the player one step in that direction if an exit exists in that direction.
- Place this D-pad below the fold area — I'll add it as a new bar under `#place-head` inside `#interact`? Hmm, "折叠下方" — below the fold button. Actually let me re-read again:

"1.赶路按钮太小，地图本来也小，要么就把移动按钮放在下面，地图依旧支持点击移动，移动按钮移动到折叠下方，做一个四项移动（上下左右）的按钮"

Translation: "The travel button is too small, and the map is also small. Either put the movement buttons below [the map], the map still supports click-move, move the movement buttons below the fold, and make a 4-directional (up/down/left/right) button."

So the design: movement buttons (D-pad with 上/下/左/右) placed below the fold (折叠) — i.e., in the interact area under the place-head (which contains the fold button). The map keeps click-to-move.

I'll add a `#move-pad` element between `#place-head` and `#place-desc` (or right below `#place-head`), containing a D-pad. When folded, the D-pad could remain visible (it's small) — the fold currently hides place-desc/npc/event/combat to give log more room. The user wants the move buttons "移动到折叠下方" — below the fold button — so they stay visible even when folded. Best placement: directly under `#place-head` inside `#interact`, before `#place-desc`. When folded, place-desc/npc/event hide but the D-pad stays.

Actually wait — maybe better: put the D-pad in a fixed position at the bottom-right of the map panel (like an overlay), since "移动按钮放在下面" could mean at the bottom. Hmm. "把移动按钮放在下面" = put the movement buttons below (the map?). "移动按钮移动到折叠下方" = move the movement buttons below the fold.

Let me go with: A D-pad strip placed inside #interact right below #place-head (which contains the fold button). This is "below the fold button". It will always be visible (not affected by folding). The D-pad has 上/下/左/右 buttons.

For the direction mapping: room exits use keys n/s/e/w. The look() function maps them: {n:'北',s:'南',e:'东',w:'西'}. So D-pad buttons: 北/南/东/西 or 上/下/左/右. The user said 上下左右 (up/down/left/right). I'll label them 上/下/左/右 with direction hints. Map:
- 上 → n (北)
- 下 → s (南)
- 左 → w (西)
- 右 → e (东)

If no exit in that direction, show a message like "（西边无路可走）".

Also the movement buttons should handle the case where moving one step: use moveTo(rn) if adjacent exit exists. But maybe the player wants to "赶路" (travel) — the request says 赶路按钮太小. Hmm, "赶路" here likely refers to the travel buttons in general (the askMove confirm buttons 疾行/逐格). The user finds the map small and buttons tiny.

So I'll:
1. Add the D-pad below the fold in #interact.
2. Make the map-tip buttons bigger? The map-tip is at bottom of the map. Actually the user said "要么就把移动按钮放在下面" — either put the movement buttons below. Since we're putting a D-pad below, the inline map-tip buttons (疾行/逐格/取消) could stay but be made larger, OR we could keep them. Let me keep the map-tip confirm (疾行/逐格/取消) — but move them? The user's phrasing: "移动按钮移动到折叠下方" — the movement buttons move below the fold. The movement buttons = the D-pad + maybe the travel confirm. I think the cleanest interpretation:

- The D-pad (4-direction) is placed below the fold.
- The map still supports click-move (askMove with 疾行/逐格 confirm stays on the map-tip, but maybe relocate).

Hmm, but "赶路按钮太小" — where's the 赶路 button? Let me search for a literal 赶路 button in the UI... There's map-travel (⟿ 传送/驿路) button. There's also 上马赶路 (mount ride). The askMove confirm has 疾行 (run) / 逐格 (walk) buttons. I think "赶路按钮" refers to these small tip buttons at the bottom-left of the map (map-tip), which are tiny (font-size .72em, padding 2px 10px).

OK here's my plan for Fix 1:
- Add a 4-direction D-pad (上/下/左/右) below the fold, i.e., directly under `#place-head` in `#interact`. Buttons are large and easy to tap.
- Move the travel-confirm (疾行/逐格/取消) buttons from the small map-tip overlay into a row inside the D-pad area? That may overcomplicate. The user says "移动按钮移动到折叠下方" — so I should move the movement/travel buttons (currently in map-tip) below the fold.

Let me re-read once more: "1.赶路按钮太小，地图本来也小，要么就把移动按钮放在下面，地图依旧支持点击移动，移动按钮移动到折叠下方，做一个四项移动（上下左右）的按钮"

Breaking down:
- 赶路按钮太小，地图本来也小 → The travel button is too small; the map is also small.
- 要么就把移动按钮放在下面 → Either put the movement buttons below (the map).
- 地图依旧支持点击移动 → The map still supports click-to-move.
- 移动按钮移动到折叠下方 → The movement buttons move below the fold.
- 做一个四项移动（上下左右）的按钮 → Make a 4-direction (up/down/left/right) button.

So: Create a 4-direction D-pad below the fold; keep map click-to-move. The D-pad is the "movement button" moved below.

I'll implement:
1. Add `#move-pad` with 4 direction buttons (上/下/左/右) + maybe a center "站" (rest?) No — keep just 4 directions. Actually a D-pad cross layout: 上 on top, 下 bottom, 左 left, 右 right. With a cross layout in a compact square. This looks like a real gamepad.

Placement: inside `#interact`, right after `#place-head`. When folded, place-desc/npc/event/combat hide but #move-pad stays visible. Also for logmax mode (fullscreen log), the D-pad would be hidden — that's fine.

Alternatively place it at the bottom-right of the map panel as a floating overlay — but "折叠下方" suggests in the interact area under the fold. I'll go with inside #interact after #place-head.

2. Keep map click-to-move: clicking a node calls askMove → for adjacent rooms moves directly, for far rooms shows confirm in map-tip. Keep that. Also enlarge map-tip buttons slightly.

3. Direction buttons call a new function `moveDir(dir)`:
```js
function moveDir(dir){
  const r=getRoom(player.room);
  if(!r||!r.exits) { log('（此处无路可走）','sys'); return; }
  const dn={n:'北',s:'南',e:'东',w:'西'};
  const target=r.exits[dir];
  if(!target){ logInfo('（'+dn[dir]+'边无路可走。）'); return; }
  moveTo(target);
  renderMap();
}
```
Wait, moveTo already calls renderMap. But adjacent moves should use askMove → moveTo directly for adjacent. Since D-pad is per-direction, moving to the exit target is by definition adjacent (one step). Use moveTo(target). Note moveTo triggers randomEncounter etc. Good.

But careful: on the zhou map level, player.room is a cheng id, and ROOMS[cheng_id] may not exist. On zhou level, movement is done by clicking city nodes (enterCheng). The D-pad should be hidden on zhou level (or disabled with message "先入城镇"). Actually on zhou level there are no directional exits between cities in the same way (CHENG_LINKS is the connectivity but exits are by enterCheng). So hide the D-pad on zhou level, show on cheng/nei levels. Let me check: game.mapLevel — 'zhou' | 'cheng' | 'nei'. I'll toggle visibility in renderMap or look().

Actually simpler: in the D-pad click handler, if lv==='zhou' show "（舆图上以城镇为途——点击城镇节点进入，或用传送）". But better to hide it. Let me add a helper to update pad visibility based on game.mapLevel in renderMap.

**Fix 2: 怎么回血，怎么使用物品，怎么穿戴装备？疗伤按钮呢？调养呢？**
- How to heal, how to use items, how to equip gear? Where's the heal button? Where's 调养 (rest/recuperate)?

There IS a 疗伤 (heal) button in the side nav (btn-heal, line 619). It calls healWoundAction which only works if wounded and requires medicine. The user says "怎么回血" — how to recover HP. The heal button only treats wounds (伤势), not HP. HP recovery options: use consumables (useItem heal), rest at inn (restAtInn, 10 gold), rest at home (restAtHome, 调养/居家休养), etc.

The user asks: add 疗伤 (heal) and 调养 (rest/recuperate) buttons that are accessible. Also how to use items and equip gear — need a backpack/inventory UI where you can click an item to use or equip.

Let me check existing UI for inventory: updateSidebar shows chips of inventory (s-inv) but no click handlers. There's useItem() function. And there was a modal at line 7852 with a select for using items — let me look at that. Let me check what's around line 7840-7860.

Also, is there an existing "背包" panel? Let me search for openBackpack or 背包.

Let me plan Fix 2:
- Add a 疗伤/调养 section: enhance the 疗伤 button (btn-heal) to also heal HP when possible (e.g., if has healing items, use them; else suggest rest). And add a 调养 (rest) button — restAtHome requires manor; restAtInn requires being at an inn room; there's a generic "打坐" maybe? Let me search for 打坐 (meditate) as a player action.

Let me search more broadly for rest/打坐/heal-related functions and the inventory UI.

**Fix 3: 地图的连线太乱了 — 重新排列所有地图，要求直线，方框平着连着方框**
- The map connections are too messy. Rearrange all maps so that lines are straight and boxes connect flat-to-flat (like a grid), not lines everywhere.

This is the big one. The map positions (CHENG_POS) are hand-placed with random-ish coordinates, and connections are drawn as straight diagonal lines between arbitrary points → messy spiderweb. The user wants a grid-like layout: boxes connected by straight horizontal/vertical lines (orthogonal), like classic MUD maps.

Approach: Instead of hand-placed coordinates, compute positions algorithmically per layer:
- For each map layer (zhou, each cheng, each bld interior), build a graph from exits.
- Lay out nodes on a grid using BFS layers (depth from entry) — assign each node (col, row) so that edges connect adjacent-ish nodes, producing straight horizontal/vertical lines between boxes.
- Draw lines as orthogonal polylines (horizontal then vertical) between box centers so lines are straight axis-aligned, boxes flat-connected.

Simpler robust approach: layered grid layout:
1. BFS from entry room to assign each node a "depth" (column = depth).
2. Within each depth column, assign rows (order). Place nodes at grid cells: x = depth*spacing, y = row*spacing.
3. Edges drawn as orthogonal paths: from box center → horizontal to mid → vertical to target row → horizontal into target. Or simpler: if target is in next column, draw an L-shaped/straight path with an elbow at the midpoint.

But pure BFS layering can still cross. However with orthogonal routing (elbows at midpoints between columns), it looks clean and "MUD-like": boxes in columns with straight horizontal/vertical lines.

Actually, even cleaner for a MUD feel: a grid where each node is a box, and connections are only drawn between adjacent boxes in the same row or column when the graph edge connects them; for non-grid-adjacent edges, route orthogonally with an elbow.

Given there are ~24 cities each with 10-60 rooms, I need a deterministic auto-layout. The user explicitly wants "重新排列所有地图" — rearrange ALL maps. So I should replace the manual CHENG_POS positions with computed grid positions for rendering. But CHENG_POS is used elsewhere (mapSize for nei bounding box, mapZoomReset, mapLocate, renderChengMap). I could:

Option A: Replace CHENG_POS data entirely with computed grid coordinates. That's a huge data change and risky (mapSize uses it, etc.). 

Option B: Keep CHENG_POS data but ignore coordinates in rendering — compute layout at render time via a function `layoutPositions(layerRooms)` that returns a room→{x,y} map, and use it in renderChengMap/renderZhouMap and in mapSize/mapZoomReset/mapLocate consistently.

Option B is cleaner: a single source of truth function `layerPos()` that computes a tidy grid layout for the current layer's rooms, cached per layer. Replace all `CHENG_POS[game.cheng]` reads in map functions with `layerPos()`.

But CHENG_POS is also used in NPC movement logic? Let me check where CHENG_POS is used elsewhere (grep found only lines 4745, 4808, 4823, 5316). 4745/4808/4823 are in mapSize/mapZoomReset/mapLocate. 5316 is renderChengMap. So all uses are map-related! Great — I can replace them all with a computed layout.

Also CHENG_CFG.pos is used in renderZhouMap and mapLocate (zhou level). I can compute zhou layout too, or keep the zhou positions (they're already nicely spread by zhou). The zhou map lines connect cities — the user says the lines are messy. The zhou map positions are manually placed and lines may cross. For a truly tidy zhou map, I'd also grid-layout the cities. Let me compute a zhou layout from CHENG_LINKS graph too.

Design for layout algorithm (per layer):
```
function computeLayout(rooms, edges, root, cellW, cellH, padX, padY)
```
1. Build adjacency list from edges (undirected).
2. BFS from root to compute depth of each node (root=0). Also compute parent for each node.
3. Group nodes by depth → columns. For each depth d, we have a list of nodes. Order nodes within a column to minimize crossings: use barycenter heuristic — order by average position of neighbors in previous column.
4. Assign grid: x(d) = padX + d*cellW; y = padY + row*cellH where row = index in column ordering (but we want rows aligned across columns so lines are straight... not strictly necessary).
5. Convert grid → pixel coordinates: x = padX + col*cellW, y = padY + row*cellH.

Then render nodes as boxes (rect) at (x,y) with size cellW×cellH... Actually boxes should be smaller than cell spacing, e.g., box 150×80 at cell 240×130.

Edges: draw orthogonal paths between box centers:
- If same column (same depth) — rare; draw vertical line.
- If adjacent columns: draw "S" path: start (x1, cy1) → (mx, cy1) → (mx, cy2) → (x2, cy2) where mx = (x1+x2)/2 = column mid. This gives straight horizontal segments and one vertical segment — clean and tidy, all axis-aligned.
- For nodes in the same row across columns, the path is a straight horizontal line (nice "方框平着连着方框" = boxes flat-connected). For different rows, it's an L/S with a vertical at the midpoint — still tidy.

To make it look like "boxes flat connected", I should draw the box borders and connect edges from box edge to box edge, not center to center. The S-path from box edges with small elbow looks fine.

Crossing minimization: order nodes within each column by barycenter of their neighbors' rows in adjacent columns, iterating a few times (like Sugiyama). This produces quite tidy layouts for typical MUD graphs.

Edge cases:
- Disconnected components (some rooms may be isolated or in separate subgraphs). BFS from root covers the main component; leftover rooms need placement — put them in extra columns after main layout or connect nearest. In the previous session they fixed broken links so graphs should be connected per layer, but let me handle leftovers by BFS from each unvisited node and append columns.
- The zhou map: root = ? Some entry like cheng_lizhu (骊珠小镇, the home town). Use that as root for zhou layout. Or keep it centered: root = home town.

For the zhou map, maybe preserve geographic intent loosely: Actually the user wants tidy lines, "方框平着连着方框" — boxes flat connected. A grid layout for zhou with boxes works. Let me use boxes (rounded rect) for cities too.

Node rendering changes: currently circles. The user says "方框平着连着方框" (boxes flat connected to boxes) — so render nodes as rounded rectangles (boxes) with labels inside. I'll change room-node circles to rects. Keep the current/hover styles. This is a bigger visual change but matches the request.

Node sizes: city boxes bigger (e.g., 170×70), room boxes (e.g., 150×54 for cheng, 140×50 for nei). Font sizes adapt.

viewBox: mapSize returns {w,h} — computed from layout bounds + padding. For cheng, previously 2600×2000 fixed; with new layout, compute from bounds. Let me update mapSize to use the computed layout size. Actually simpler: compute layout first (cached), then mapSize returns bounds. I need a function `currentLayerLayout()` that returns {pos: {room:{x,y}}, w, h, cx, cy}.

Since mapZoomReset for cheng uses s=3 and focuses player room, and mapLocate centers on player room — with computed positions these still work via the layout map.

Let me also handle the back gate node at (0,0) — applyMapView pins it at viewport top-left. With new coordinates starting at pad (e.g., 200), the gate at (0,0) is fine.

Now, the nei (building interior) layout: rooms inside a building, e.g., 客栈大堂/客房/后厨. Compute layout from those rooms' exits with root = the building's main room? The interior rooms' exits connect to each other and possibly back to outside room? Let me check how interior rooms are structured — exits of interior rooms probably connect to other interior rooms only. The layerRooms for nei = rooms with bld===game.bld. Compute layout from those. Root = first room or the room the player is in.

Let me check ROOMS structure for exits keys on interior rooms, e.g. '骊珠小镇·平安客栈·大堂'. I'll trust exits exist.

**Fix 4: 删除输入帮助，现在根本用不着输入了为什么还要有个输入框**
- Delete input help; there's no input needed anymore, why is there still an input box?

3. Keep processCommand? It's dead code now. The user says "现在根本用不着输入了为什么还要有个输入框" — the complaint is about the input box. If there's no input box, the help text referencing input is confusing. **Fix 5: 地图移动文本太长**
- Map movement text too long.

This refers to the move confirm text: showMoveConfirm sets `'前往「'+label+'」· '+steps+' 程（脚力 '+fp+' 程）'` plus 3 buttons — the map-tip has max-width:86% and nowrap ellipsis, so text gets cut. Also walkPath logs "（你决定一步一步走过去——N 程的路，不急着赶。）" and per-step "（你行至「rn」，脚步不停……）". The user says 地图移动文本太长 — map movement text too long. - Also walkPath log messages shorten: "（你决定一步步走过去——N 程的路。）" and step message "（行至「rn」…）". Actually the "地图移动文本" likely = the map-tip text (map movement text). I'll shorten showMoveConfirm and showWalkTip (progress text 🚶 逐格步行 · d/total 程（pct%）→ shorter). Let me shorten both the tip and the related log lines moderately.

const parts=t.split(/\s+/); const cmd=parts[0]; const args=parts.slice(1);
log('（战斗中可用：攻击 / 施展 武功名 / 使用 物品名 / 防御 / 激将·规劝·以理服人 嘴遁 / 逃走）','sys'); return;
if(!args.length){ log('（用法：对话 人物名）','sys'); return; }
if(game.npcDead[who]){ log('（此人已不在人世）','sys'); return; }
if(npcCurrentRoom(who)!==player.room){ log('（'+who+'此刻不在此处，去别处寻他吧）','sys'); return; }
if(cmd==='steal'||cmd==='偷'){ if(args.length){ if(npcCurrentRoom(args.join(' '))===player.room) stealFrom(args.join(' ')); else log('（不在此处）','sys'); } else log('（用法：偷 人物名）','sys'); return; }
if(cmd==='fight'||cmd==='战'){ if(args.length) startFight(args.join(' ')); else log('（用法：战斗 敌人名）','sys'); return; }
if(cmd==='use'||cmd==='使用'){ if(args.length) useItem(args.join(' ')); else log('（用法：使用 物品名）','sys'); return; }
if(cmd==='travel'||cmd==='驿'||cmd==='传送'){ if(args.length) doTravel(args.join(' ')); else openTravel(); return; }
logDiv(); logTitle('—— 剑来 · 指令说明 ——');
log('【地图】三级舆图：洲舆图点城镇入内，城镇内点建筑入内（有内部的建筑），左上「↑返回」回上一级。点地点弹出「行路」：相邻抬脚即走，远途可脚程疾行或逐格步行——移动耗时随脚力：步行两时辰/格，轻功一个时辰，骑乘坐骑只需半个时辰。','sys');
log('【人物】下方「人物」栏点击可对话，对话后可拜师、购买、送礼、求婚等。','sys');
log('【事件】下方「事件」栏会显示当前可触发的剧情，选项不同后果不同。','sys');
log('【战斗】点「战 敌人」进入独立战斗场景——攻、法、守、言、走五路；环境借势（雷泽雷法大增、雪域寒刃逞威、沙海火旺水竭），嘴遁三式可破敌可退兵。','sys');
log('【公式】气血=基础+20/级+境界与体修筑基；内力=基础+10/级+境界与练气筑基；减伤率=防御/(防御+80)，另加装备与铁布衫加成；会心=5%+0.3%/级+装备词条+暗器身法流派；暴伤默认150%，剑修辅修每层+2%。','sys');
log('【好感】好感分五段：萍水相逢→初识→相见恨晚→肝胆相照→生死之交，越亲近越难更进一步；「谈天论道」可探心事、「旁敲侧击」可打听喜好，投其所好，事半功倍；送错东西是会恼的。','sys');
log('【世界】江湖是活的：NPC会赶路、访友、切磋、受重伤，也会结仇寻仇；每五回合一条「江湖动态」。','sys');
log('【奇遇】静态奇遇演尽之后，人间万象照常展开——劫道、走失、遗物、伤者、骤雨……永远有新事发生。','sys');
log('【生成】每一档新江湖都有一把新世界种子：人物、任务、喜好各各不同；读旧档仍是旧人旧事。','sys');
log('【技艺】「技艺」面板有四门手艺：铁匠（打造/淬炼）、炼丹（丹方/火候）、种植（需田产）、鉴宝（蒙尘物件搏机缘）——手艺越练越精。','sys');
log('【功法】天下功法分剑法/刀法/拳掌/道法/符箓/暗器/雷法诸流派，由低而高：基础招数易得，绝学难求。','sys');
log('【宗门】拜师入门后，掌门处可开「宗门大殿」：办宗门事务攒贡奉、以贡奉兑器物学艺、修各宗专属功课（儒门功名/佛门功德/剑道剑意/纵横军略）。宗门之间亦有交好与交恶。','sys');

log('【容貌】容貌三分天生、七分打点：胭脂巷的温轻眉处可买丹换衣、授易容驻颜之术；容貌于好感有微妙助益，也会招来无赖的觊觎——以容貌周旋，也以容貌立身。','sys');
log('【关系】侧栏「关系」可翻人情簿：结为好友可邀同游（谈天不限、嘴遁帮腔）；红颜知己可听知心话、逢难相救；恩人当记，仇人血债自有公论——好感到了，皆可变作情义。','sys');
log('【岁月】六回合一季，二十四回合一载——四季风物轮转，顶部历法可见。通关之后，天下大事由自生成器轮番上演（妖祸、盟主大会、秘境、商路、祥瑞、灾祸、讲学、正邪论剑），可参与、可观望，皆入编年史册。','sys');
log('【存亡】覆灭级大事件亦会降临：某宗被围、某城被攻——不救，便灭。守住了酬以威名，没守住则宗门覆灭（掌门陨落/门人四散）或城池陷落（废墟/妖兵盘踞），可在「世界大事」中筹募复兴：中兴宗门、光复城池。','sys');
log('【财货】侧栏「财货」管着钱袋子：银两、灵石（仙家硬通货，行情随世道波动 ±），矿产行情日日不同——骊珠矿洞可下井采矿，矿石可当市价变现；灵石可灌顶修炼、淬炼保底、补复兴耗材，也能在「灵石私市」淘珍品与功法残卷。','sys');
log('【簿册】「名望」面板可翻成就·江湖簿：初试锋芒到问鼎天下，十六桩轶事记你一路刀痕；街头不时有说书人开讲，江湖奇谈里，说不定就有你一段。','sys');
log('【传书与运势】故人常来信：好友、红颜知己、配偶都会寄来问候（或夹带私礼），拆阅记得回信；「财货」里可花 20 两问一卦吉凶，四回合内应验于前路。','sys');

Line 3297:   '店小二':{ title:'云来客栈小二', gender:'男', aff:40, home:'云来客栈', canKill:true, hp:50,atk:8,def:3, loot:['干粮'], quest:'打听', greet:'客官里边请！', talk:'小店提供歇脚，花费十两银便可养足精神。客官要是肯帮我打探个消息，这顿酒钱我请你。', likes:['干粮'], service:'rest' },
Line 3306:   '阿良':{ title:'亚圣之子·道理剑', gender:'男', aff:20, home:'剑气长城入口', roams:['剑气长城入口','云来客栈','宝瓶洲渡口','小镇官道','沙海绿洲','剑气长城城头'], canKill:false, quest:'斗酒', greet:'（男人靠着墙根喝酒，闻言大笑）我叫阿良，善良的良！', talk:'江湖没什么好的，也就是酒好。你若能寻一壶陈年女儿红来，我这一手「道理剑」，便教给你。', likes:['陈年女儿红'] },
Line 3310:   '朱敛':{ title:'落魄山大管家', gender:'男', aff:25, home:'落魄山', roams:['落魄山','云来客栈','藕花福地'], canKill:true, hp:70,atk:12,def:8, loot:['干粮','谷雨钱'], greet:'（温润如玉的男子执扇而笑）落魄山朱敛，恭候多时。', talk:'我是落魄山的大管家，山上山下，柴米油盐，皆归我管。你若无处落脚，落魄山的门槛，向来是开着的。', likes:['干粮','谷雨钱'] },
Line 3317:   '刘羡阳':{ title:'少年侠客', gender:'男', aff:25, home:'云来客栈', roams:['云来客栈','大骊京城','小镇官道','宝瓶洲渡口','荒郊野岭'], canKill:true, hp:75,atk:13,def:7, loot:['陈年女儿红','干粮'], greet:'（豪爽少年拍桌大笑）兄弟，喝一杯？', talk:'我叫刘羡阳，天不怕地不怕。这江湖啊，只要有酒有朋友，哪儿都能闯。你要是有意思，咱们一起走江湖！', likes:['陈年女儿红','干粮'] },
Line 3318:   '陈灵均':{ title:'落魄山左护法·水蛟', gender:'男', aff:20, home:'宝瓶洲渡口', roams:['宝瓶洲渡口','大骊京城','云来客栈','蛮荒密林'], canKill:true, hp:80,atk:14,def:8, loot:['蛇胆石','疗伤丹'], greet:'（青衣小童叉腰，奶声奶气却老气横秋）本护法在此，还不速速拜见？', talk:'本座陈灵均，御江水蛟化形，落魄山左护法！百斤体重，九十七斤都是义气！你请我喝酒，我便护着你！', likes:['陈年女儿红','蛇胆石'] },
Line 3331:   '宁姚':{ title:'剑仙之女', gender:'女', aff:20, home:'云来客栈', roams:['云来客栈','剑气长城入口','剑气长城城头'], canKill:false, beauty:true, charm:92, greet:'（斗笠下，一双清冷的眼看了过来）……', talk:'剑气长城之女，宁姚。江湖险恶，我劝你莫要趟这浑水。若你非要闯，便去那剑气长城，见识见识真正的风浪。', likes:['疗伤丹','仙家雪莲'], marry:true, mysterious:true },
Line 3340:   '郭竹酒':{ title:'落魄山的小丫头', gender:'女', aff:30, home:'落魄山', roams:['落魄山','集灵峰','小镇官道','云来客栈'], canKill:true, hp:35,atk:6,def:2, loot:['干粮','草药'], beauty:true, charm:70, quest:'灵鸟', greet:'（扎着羊角辫的小丫头叉腰拦路）此山是我开，此树是我栽！', talk:'我是郭竹酒！我可算得是山主座下……的小师叔，才怪啦。不过我偷看过他练剑，可厉害了！你带我去吃酒，我讲给你听！', likes:['干粮','陈年女儿红'] },

block.text:
Now I understand the healing system. Key issues:

1. `healAction()` calls `healWoundAction()` which requires: wound>0 AND has medicine. If no medicine → "手边没有伤药" — useless. If no wound but HP low → "并无伤势" — useless.
2. `healWoundAction` only heals wounds, not HP directly.
3. No natural HP regen over time (dayTick has no HP recovery).
4. `restAction()` requires manor or inn room or meditate fallback (25% hp/mp, cd 6).

The user's request: "疗伤不应该必须要有药什么的，增加更多治疗方式" — healing should not require medicine; add more healing methods. And "寻找更多的诸如没有疗伤功能的硬伤" — find more hard bugs like the non-functional healing.

So the plan:
1. **Rework `healAction()`** to be a comprehensive healing that works without medicine:
   - If wounded and has medicine → use it (敷药)
   - Else if HP low → 运功疗伤 (spend MP to heal HP) — no medicine needed
   - Also 打坐调息 fallback
2. **Add natural HP/MP regeneration** in `dayTick()` — each day recovers some HP/MP (like classic MUDs).
3. **Add 运功疗伤 (meditate-to-heal)** — spend MP to restore HP, always available, no medicine.
4. **More healing methods**:
   - 客栈歇宿 (rest at inn, 10 gold) — exists
   - 居家调养 (rest at home) — exists
   - 运功疗伤 (new) — spend MP to heal HP
   - 打坐调息 (meditate) — in restAction fallback
   - natural regen per day (new)
5. **Audit for more hard bugs** — features that don't work. Let me look at the ones I can find quickly:
   - `healWoundAction` — no medicine → useless
   - Check `restAtInn` — requires being at inn? It doesn't check room, just gold and reputation. Actually `restAtInn` works anywhere (just gold). My `restAction` checks room name contains 客栈/客房/驿馆, else falls to meditate.
   - Let me check `updateWound` — it auto-derives wound from HP ratio, so healing HP reduces wound automatically. Good.

Let me now design the improved healing:

```js
// —— 运功疗伤：消耗内力自行疗伤（无需药物） ——
function qiHeal(){
  if(battleMode){ log('（战事未了，先顾眼前）','sys'); return; }
  if(game._walking){ logInfo('（你正在赶路——到了地方再歇吧）'); return; }
  const maxHp=effMaxHp();
  if(player.hp>=maxHp && player.mp>=effMaxMp() && player.wound<=0){ log('（你气血充盈，无需疗伤。）','sys'); return; }
  const mpCost=Math.max(10, Math.floor(player.mp*0.2)); // 耗内力
  if(player.mp<10){ log('（内力不足，难以运功——可歇息调养或服丹药。）','sys'); return; }
  player.mp-=mpCost;
  const gain=Math.floor(maxHp*0.2)+player.level*2;
  player.hp=Math.min(maxHp, player.hp+gain);
```

block.text:
Now I understand the current leveling system:
- `checkLevelUp()` — auto-levels when exp >= expNeeded. On realm boundary crossing, it just applies the realm bonus (with a possible heart-demon trial at 35% chance).
- Realms are tied to `player.level` thresholds — pure auto-upgrade. No breakthrough ceremony, no requirements, no choice of path.

The user wants:
1. 增加和丰富修炼系统 (enrich the cultivation system)
2. 增加练功方式 (add training methods)
3. 增加经验获取方式 (add XP sources)
4. 优化突破/破境的体验 (optimize breakthrough experience)
5. 增加破境的要求 (add breakthrough requirements)
6. 提供多种晋升路径 (multiple promotion paths): 丹药 (pills), 灌顶 (spiritual infusion), 感悟 (comprehension), 顿悟 (sudden enlightenment), 境界到了 (realm reached)
7. 不能到了等级就直接升级到什么金丹 (no more auto-level to 金丹 — must break through deliberately)

So the core change: leveling up gives XP/level, but **realm breakthrough** (破境/境界) must be a deliberate act with requirements and multiple methods. Instead of auto-applying realm bonus at level thresholds, the player must use the 修炼 (cultivation) panel to attempt a breakthrough, which requires:
- Level requirement (reached)
- Plus one of several paths:
  - 丹药 (pills — e.g., 破境丹/培元丹/九转金丹)
  - 灌顶 (spiritual infusion — find a senior/teacher to transmit power, costs favor/gold)
  - 感悟 (comprehension — spend time in specific locations, require 悟性/洞察)
  - 顿悟 (sudden enlightenment — random chance from battles/sights/insights)
  - 水到渠成 (natural breakthrough — just requires level + some threshold, maybe with lower success)

Breakthrough should have success chance, failure consequences (injured, 走火入魔 risk), and maybe the heart-demon trial.

Now I understand the cultivation system. Let me look at `cultivateCycle`, `daoProgress`, and understand the exp gain methods. Then design the breakthrough system.

The user's request:
1. 增加和丰富修炼系统 - enrich cultivation system
2. 增加练功方式 - add more training methods  
3. 增加经验获取方式 - add more exp acquisition methods
4. 优化突破/破境的体验 - optimize breakthrough/realm-break experience
5. 增加破境的要求 - add requirements for breaking through realms
6. 提供多种晋升路径 - multiple promotion paths: 丹药(pills), 灌顶(spiritual infusion), 感悟(enlightenment/comprehension), 顿悟(sudden enlightenment), 境界到了(realm reached), etc.
7. 不能到了等级就直接升级到什么金丹 - can't just reach a level and auto-advance to Jindan etc.

So the core complaint: currently `checkLevelUp()` auto-advances realm when `player.level >= REALMS[r].lv`. The user wants a deliberate **breakthrough (破境)** system: reaching the level should NOT auto-advance the realm; instead the player must perform a breakthrough ceremony with requirements and multiple methods.

Let me design this carefully:

**Current system:**
- `REALMS[i].lv` = level threshold
- `realmIndex()` returns highest realm where `player.level >= lv`
- `checkLevelUp()` auto-applies realm bonuses when level crosses threshold (with occasional 心魔劫 at 35% chance)

**New design:**
- Leveling up (经验→等级) still gives attribute points and small stat growth.
- But **realm advancement becomes a deliberate action** ("破境"): when your level reaches `REALMS[next].lv`, you are "瓶颈期" (at a bottleneck). You must open the 修炼 panel and perform 破境.
- Multiple paths to break through:
  1. **水到渠成 (natural)**: spend 修为 (exp) + time to break through, with a success chance based on 悟性/根骨; failure = lose exp, no realm gain.
  2. **丹药 (pills)**: consume a realm-breaking pill (e.g., 破境丹/凝元丹) — guaranteed or high chance.
  3. **灌顶 (spiritual infusion)**: pay a senior NPC or spend 灵石 — like existing 灵石灌顶 but for realm breakthrough.
  4. **感悟 (comprehension)**: go to a special location (e.g., 落魄山集灵峰, 龙虎山, 剑气长城) to comprehend — requires visiting.
  5. **顿悟 (sudden enlightenment)**: random chance during battle/events/natural 周天 cycles.
- Failure consequences: 走火入魔 (qi deviation) — lose HP, wound, or exp; or bottleneck persists.
- 心魔劫 (heart demon tribulation) — keep existing but make it a required step for higher realms.

Implementation plan (minimal invasive but complete):
1. Add `player.realmLock` / `game.realmReady` tracking? Better: compute "next realm" from level; if `level >= next.lv` and current realm index < that index, player is at bottleneck: `realmIndex()` should NOT auto-advance. Instead, we add `player.breakthrough` state: `{target: realmIndex, method, cd}` or simply a flag `game.realmBlocked`.

Simplest approach that satisfies "不能到了等级就直接升级到什么金丹":
- Change `realmIndex()` to return the realm for which BOTH `player.level >= lv` AND breakthrough done. We add `player.brokenRealms = [true]` array (index 0 always true). `realmIndex()` = highest r where `player.level >= REALMS[r].lv && (player.brokenRealms[r] === true)`.
- `checkLevelUp()` no longer applies realm bonuses automatically; instead, when crossing a threshold, it sets a flag/message "境界瓶颈——可至「修炼」面板破境" and keeps stats unchanged until breakthrough happens.
- Add `openBreakthrough()` in the 修炼 panel: shows next realm, requirements, and the multiple paths.

Let me check how `realmApplied` is used and how stats get applied on breakthrough, and what `ensureOrigin` is, plus `PATHS` and `daoProgress`. Also need to handle: 元婴 requirement (寿命), chapter gating, etc.

Also need to preserve existing save compat: old saves won't have `player.brokenRealms` — initialize it to all realms up to current realmIndex (auto-marked done) so old saves don't break.

Also `realmName()` uses PATHS[player.path].realms — path-specific realm names! Let me look at PATHS.

Let me also check `autoAllocateAttrs`, `ensureOrigin`, `checkChapterProgress`, and how `player.level` interacts with things like `expNeeded`. And check `applyStartup` which sets initial realm (START_REALMS with lv>1) — those start at higher levels so should mark realms done.

This is getting complex. Let me be careful and systematic. Let me read PATHS, START_REALMS, ensureOrigin, daoProgress, cultivateCycle.
This is a significant system change. Let me study the remaining relevant pieces: `PATHS`, `START_REALMS`, `cultivateCycle`, `ensureOrigin`, and `daoProgress`:

block.text:
Now I have a good understanding of the system. Let me now design the breakthrough system overhaul:

Current state:
- `checkLevelUp()` auto-levels and auto-applies realm bonuses when level crosses `REALMS[r].lv` thresholds. The user complains: "不能到了等级就直接升级到什么金丹" — you shouldn't automatically advance realms just by reaching a level.

The user wants:
1. 增加和丰富修炼系统 — enrich cultivation system
2. 增加练功方式 — more training methods
3. 增加经验获取方式 — more XP acquisition methods
4. 优化突破/破境的体验 — optimize breakthrough experience
5. 增加破境的要求 — add breakthrough requirements
6. 提供多种晋升路径 — multiple advancement paths: 丹药 (pills), 灌顶 (spiritual infusion), 感悟 (comprehension), 顿悟 (sudden enlightenment), 境界到了 (realm reached naturally)
7. 不能到了等级就直接升级到什么金丹 — no more auto realm-up at level thresholds

Design plan:

**Core change**: Split "level" from "realm". Levels still grow with XP (attribute points, small stat gains), but **realm advancement becomes a deliberate act** — a 破境 (breakthrough) ceremony with requirements and multiple methods.

Implementation:
1. Add `game.realmGate` tracking: when player's level reaches the next realm's `lv` threshold, mark the realm as "pending breakthrough" (`game.pendingRealm = index`). `realmIndex()` should only count realms that have been **broken through** (or start at realm 0).
   - Add `player.realmsBroken = []` array or a flag `game.realmBroken[i]`? Better: track `game.realmBroken = {realmIdx: true}` or simply `player.realmTier` = the highest realm index actually achieved through breakthrough.
   - Simplest robust approach: keep `realmIndex()` based on level BUT gate the **bonuses** behind a breakthrough flag. Actually cleanest: introduce `player.breakthrough = N` where N = highest realm index the player has formally broken through. `realmIndex()` returns min(level-based index, N)... no wait, the user wants: you can't BE 金丹 just because your level is high enough; you must perform the breakthrough.

Let me design concretely:

- `player.level` grows with XP as before (gives +2 attr points, +20 HP, +10 MP, +2 ATK, +1 DEF per level). That's fine — that's "修为精进".
- Add `player.realmIdx` (default 0 = 市井凡俗). This is the ACTUAL realm the player has achieved.
- `REALMS[i].lv` now means "level required to attempt breaking through to realm i".
- When `player.level >= REALMS[realmIdx+1].lv` and realmIdx+1 exists → show "破境在即" and offer a breakthrough ceremony via the 修炼 panel (and a floating hint in the log).
- `realmIndex()` → returns `player.realmIdx`.
- `realmApplied()` → sums bonuses for realms 0..player.realmIdx (unchanged, just driven by realmIdx).
- `realmName()` → uses player.realmIdx.

**Breakthrough methods** (multiple paths):
1. **水到渠成 / 境界到了 (natural breakthrough)**: requires level >= next.lv AND 悟性 (wisdom) or 根骨 threshold, plus spend XP (e.g., 1.5× current expNeeded) and some time (advanceTime). Success chance based on attributes; on failure lose the XP and get a cooldown. Classic MUD.

Now I have a complete picture. Let me design the breakthrough system:

**Current behavior**: `realmIndex()` auto-derives from `player.level` — reaching the level threshold auto-breaks through to the realm (with a 35% chance of 心魔劫). The user says "不能到了等级就直接升级到什么金丹" — can't just level up and automatically be Golden Core.

**New design**:
1. `player.level` still grows with XP (layer 层数 = raw level).
2. **Realm (境界) is separate**: `player.realm` tracks the actual realm achieved. Realm advancement requires a deliberate "破境/突破" action with requirements and multiple methods.
3. Level up no longer auto-applies realm bonuses. Instead, when the player's level crosses a realm threshold, they're "境界到了，但未破境" — they can attempt breakthrough.
4. Multiple breakthrough paths:
   - **水到渠成 (natural)**: just requires level reached + spending some 修为 (exp) — like now but gated behind a button, maybe with a cooldown / minor cost.
   - **丹药 (pill)**: consume a breakthrough pill (need new items: 破境丹/凝元丹/九转金丹?) — guaranteed or high chance.
   - **灌顶 (spiritual infusion)**: spend 灵石 / have a senior NPC transmit — e.g. 灵石灌顶 with higher cost.
   - **感悟 (comprehension)**: require visiting certain locations or completing certain actions, accumulate 感悟 points via training; when 感悟 full, breakthrough succeeds.
   - **顿悟 (sudden enlightenment)**: random chance from battles/events — auto-breaks through.
5. Breakthrough has a success chance + failure consequences (loss of exp, wound, cooldown) unless using guaranteed method.
6. 心魔劫 (heart demon) becomes part of the breakthrough attempt (maybe for higher realms).

This is a big feature. Let me keep it well-scoped but complete:

**Implementation plan**:

1. Add `player.realm` (index of achieved realm, default 0). Add migration in `loadGame`/`freshGame`/`applyStartup`: if `player.realm === undefined`, compute from level (legacy behavior) so old saves don't break.

2. Change `realmIndex()` to return `player.realm` instead of computing from level. But careful — many places use `realmIndex()` for gameplay (death, age, origin, etc.). That's fine — realm is now the actual achievement.

Wait, but there's a subtlety: level-based bonuses. `realmApplied()` sums bonuses for realms 0..realmIndex. If realm < level-derived index, bonuses are smaller. That's the point — you must actually break through.

3. `checkLevelUp()`: remove the auto-realm-break block. Instead:
   - Level up normally (HP/MP/atk/def/attrPts).
   - If `realmNextAvailable()` (level >= next realm's lv), log "破境在即" hint and set `game.realmReady = true` so the 修炼 panel shows the breakthrough UI.
   - 心魔劫 can be triggered as part of breakthrough attempts (keep existing mechanics but hook them into the new flow, or keep the random 心魔 as a flavor during breakthrough).

4. Add breakthrough UI in `openCultPanel()`:
   - Show current realm, next realm, requirements (level, plus maybe 悟性/机缘).
   - Buttons:
     a. **水到渠成** (natural breakthrough): cost exp (e.g. 40% of expNeeded), success chance ~60%+wisdom bonus; failure: lose the exp, wound+1, cooldown 8 turns.
     b. **丹药破境**: consume '破境丹' (new item, alchemy recipe) → guaranteed (or 90%).
     c. **灌顶破境**: spend N 灵石 (e.g. 5) → guaranteed.
     d. **感悟破境**: requires 感悟 points (game.realize, gained from training/周天/观景). When 感悟 >= 100, guaranteed.
     e. **顿悟**: random trigger — after battles/events, small chance to set game.insight → auto breakthrough next time or free breakthrough button.
   
   To keep scope manageable, I'll implement:
   - `game.realmReady` flag
   - 水到渠成 (cost exp, chance-based)
   - 丹药破境 (new item 破境丹 + alchemy recipe)
   - 灌顶破境 (灵石 cost)
   - 顿悟 (random from level-up or battle with 机缘-based chance → free breakthrough)
   - 感悟 (add `game.realize` points from 周天搬运 and 观景/事件; 感悟满 → guaranteed breakthrough)

5. New items: 破境丹 (breakthrough pill, consumable effect 'break'). Add alchemy recipe. Maybe 凝元丹 for higher tiers — keep single pill tiered by realm: pill works if realm index <= some threshold; or make two pills (破境丹 for ≤天象, 凝元丹 for higher).

6. Add more training methods (练功方式) and XP sources:
   - The 修炼 panel already has 周天搬运 (cycle), 灵石灌顶, 自创功法.
   - Add: 静坐悟道 (meditate, no MP cost, small XP, adds 感悟), 观景悟道 (requires being at scenic spots?), 吐纳 (breathing, free small XP).
   - XP sources already rich (hunts, quests, battles, trade, estates). Add: 打坐 (new), 听道/读书 (maybe existing), keep focus on 修炼 panel expansion.

7. Requirements for breaking through (破境要求): 
   - Level >= next realm lv (existing)
